changes: The simulator pane grows real controls: Home, Lock and Rotate on its bar, a field naming the running app that launches any installed app by bundle id (or opens a deep link), and a badge reading the OS and screen size that follows rotation.
While a simulator is open, ⌘K carries a Device group — Open app or URL, Relaunch, Home, Lock, Rotate, Shake, Copy screenshot — with window shortcuts ⌘L, ⌘R, ⌘⇧H and ⌘⇧R, all listed in the ⌘? sheet.
Clicking to edit no longer flickers: the cursor appears directly on the line you clicked instead of visibly leaping there a frame later.
Clicking into a wrapped paragraph, code fence, or quote puts the cursor on the exact line you aimed at, and revealing a block always scrolls it into view.
The document now edits like one continuous field: arrow keys cross block edges, backspace and delete join blocks, and the cursor keeps its column moving between them.
Undo finally survives leaving a block: ⌃Z steps back through your typing, then on through every fold, checkbox toggle, and join — ⌃Y redoes.
Search shows its work: stepping matches reveals the match highlighted in place, and browsing a document can never modify it.
When a file changed on disk underneath you, ⌃R takes the disk version (⌃S still keeps yours) — and quitting no longer silently overwrites the other writer.
Links jump to #section headings, the outline opens on the section you're reading and is clickable, ⌘S saves without closing your editor, and a new empty file can simply be typed into.
Arrow keys in the markdown editor now move through a wrapped paragraph line by line as it appears on screen, instead of jumping straight to the next block.
The markdown scrollbar can no longer get stuck on screen: a fast flick that outran the pointer now ends the drag cleanly, and the bar folds away as it should.
Markdown documents wrap their text: long paragraphs now break inside the reading column instead of running off the right edge of the page.
The markdown viewer's scrollbar is now Safari-style: invisible while you read, a slim pill while you scroll, wider and brighter under the pointer, and draggable anywhere on its track.

Markdown sessions work again: the bundled synth-md runtime shipped signed without its JIT entitlements, so every document row opened and instantly closed. The runtime is now signed correctly, and a release whose runtime cannot start aborts instead of shipping.

Cmd+clicking a link that carries a bare file path (no file:// scheme, e.g. /tmp/notes.md) now opens it like any other file link — markdown lands in a Synth session — instead of the OS's bare "application can't be opened" dialog.

Leaving comment mode now parks your unsent browser comments instead of deleting them — the pins and the island stay on the page, shrunk to "2 comments not sent · Resume · Send". Only sending, deleting a row, or leaving a composer blank removes a comment.
Parked comments survive the page reloading underneath you — including the reload caused by the agent's own edit — with each pin re-finding its element.
The comment composer no longer loses clicks to the page it floats over, and a delivered batch now clears its pins and count instead of keeping them forever.

0.29.0's markdown viewer is actually in the box this time. The release built on a machine missing the viewer's dependencies, and the pipeline treated the resulting hole as a warning — so the feature announced below shipped disabled. The build now installs those dependencies itself, and a release refuses to ship without the viewer aboard.

Markdown is a session. Cmd+click any .md link in a terminal — or run `synth <file>` — and the document opens rendered in a pane beside the agent that wrote it, in an Obsidian-style live preview: click a block to see its raw markdown, click away and it re-renders. Checkboxes toggle with a click, lists continue themselves, edits autosave, and an agent rewriting the file underneath you never costs your keystrokes. ⌃F searches, ⌃O jumps by heading, and relative .md links navigate in place with a back stack.

Settings → Markdown chooses what a .md file opens in: Synth's viewer, any terminal editor on your machine (nvim, helix, micro, nano, … — found on your login shell's PATH, hosted in a Synth session), or the system default. Clicking a markdown link could previously raise a bare "The application can't be opened." when no app claimed .md files — that path is gone.

The terminal cursor now hollows out when it isn't taking keys — an unfocused pane, or any pane while Synth is in the background, shows an empty, unblinking block instead of a filled one, so the pane that will receive your typing is always the one with the solid cursor.

Clicking a file link in the terminal now opens the file. Claude Code's links carry a line number inside the path and sometimes a hostname, which macOS rejected with a bare "-50" dialog — both are resolved before the file opens, and a link to a file no longer on disk raises a toast naming the path instead of a numeric error.

In tabs mode, hovering a branch row opens a card beside it that unpacks what the row hides: the branch's sessions one level deep, each drawn with the rail's own icon and state mark so the card can never disagree with the sidebar, a fact per session only where a real counter exists (step 4/6, 18 failed), and one branch line carrying the PR number and diffstat. It is read-only and lets clicks pass straight through to the row beneath — a beat to appear cold, near-instant when moving between branches, tracking its row as you scroll and gone the moment you drag, leave or press Esc.
Tabs sit on the content's own left edge. The strip inset its chips 8px while the session card below used 14px, so every tab started 6px left of the content it belongs to.

An iOS simulator is a session, behind a new Experimental toggle (off by default). Pick a device when you start a session and its live screen streams straight into the pane — Simulator.app never launches — with your clicks, typing and scrolling delivered as real device input, and Home/Lock on the pane itself. Agents get the same device through a synth-simulator MCP server: boot, launch, tap, type, scroll, rotate, screenshot, and a describe tool that reads the screen as text — a fraction of a screenshot's size, carrying the identifiers a screenshot makes you guess at. Comment mode works here too: click an element on the device and it lands with the owning agent.

One coat, no seams. The sidebar's tint, rounded corner and shadow are gone, along with every shell hairline — the sidebar seam, the pane-header rule, the line above the sidebar foot. The window is a single surface with exactly one raised thing on it, the session card, and the card's left edge is the boundary: it doubles as the sidebar-resize grab, thickening on hover along its straight run and stopping where the corner radius begins.

Tabs mode's top row sits on one centre line. The rail tightens from 42px to 36px so the clearance around the tab run matches the clearance inside it, and the traffic lights and sidebar toggle come down to the chips' own centre line instead of holding the taller band's. The open tab's lift finally reads in dark mode too — a top highlight and tight contact shadow replace a black drop shadow that vanished against an already-dark rail.

Pasting an enormous clipboard into a rename, search or template field no longer hangs the app — the unbounded fields were forcing the whole string through text layout on every keystroke, measured at an 18-second stall.

Tabs are chips on a rail. The strip stops being one solid band welded to the window — each tab is a chip sitting on the rail, and the open one lifts off it as a card, which is the whole of what open means: no seam, no bottom bar, no fill running to the window edge. A split's panes are a hairline tray around their chips rather than a filled well, because on this strip a background is what open means, so filling the tray handed every pane the one signal reserved for the open tab. Panes now shrink on the same terms as every other tab, which is the premise — a pane is a tab.

Light mode is legible inside the agents, not just around them. Claude Code was painting its dark theme onto a near-white surface — body text at 1.06:1, 57 of 72 colours under the readable threshold — because it reads its theme once at startup, so the old sync only ever reached new sessions. Synth now ships a theme it rewrites in place, which re-themes a session already running, with 20 light values deepened by lightness alone so the hues stay Claude Code's. opencode gets 11 values deepened the same way. agy paints hard-coded colour, so it is left on its default scheme — that one draws most of its interface from Synth's own ANSI palette, which is tuned further than agy's light theme is.

Settings ▸ Archived is somewhere you can stand. The clean-up switch and grace period move in beside two disk budgets (25 worktrees, 50 GB), and every project lists the folders still on disk carrying the sweeper's own verdict on each — "PR still open", "6 days left" — with Restore and a permanent delete beside them. A budget can bring an unblocked folder's turn forward; it never lets one past a gate. ⌘K's archived list is project-scoped now and drills in.

A downloaded update waits in the sidebar foot instead of interrupting you. A "Restart to update" row washed in the app icon's champagne stands above Settings for as long as a built update sits unapplied, and the notification card that used to announce it is gone — both surfaces are pull now. Settings also drops its ⌘, hint; the shortcut is unchanged, and still in ⌘? and ⌘K.

In tabs mode a branch tells you what is inside it. Sessions live in the tab strip there, so the branch is the deepest row in the sidebar — it now spends the freed chevron space on a second line reading how many sessions it holds and what they are doing, instead of hiding the count in a tooltip. Pull-request state and the branch's most urgent session state sit in two fixed slots on the right, reserved even when empty, so nothing shifts as branches change. Classic sidebar mode is untouched.

The window is translucent, terminal included — your wallpaper blurs behind the whole shell rather than stopping at the chrome. The blur carries no tint of its own, so light mode stays light instead of going grey, and the terminal participates in the effect rather than sitting on it as an opaque slab. Dark carries a little more opacity than light, because the same amount of light landing on near-black reads far stronger than on near-white.

Menu bar text is back to the weight every other app draws it at. 0.23.0's lighter text was a setting read per process, so switching it off thinned Synth's own menu bar along with its chrome — the app's chrome now reads about 12% heavier than the design files, which is the price of the OS drawing that text.

Synth is set in Geist, and the twelve text sizes that lived between 9px and 15px — most half a pixel apart — are six that are at least a pixel apart. Tracking, leading and weights are now the designs' own numbers rather than a calibration for the system face, so text sits where it was drawn to sit and reads about 12% lighter than it did.

Closing a session hands you its neighbour in the same branch, and never takes you outside it. The old rule popped to the last session you happened to view, which could be another branch or another project entirely — so two identical closes landed in different repos. An emptied branch now stops at an empty pane that names it and offers ⌘N.

An archived branch always has a way back. Restoring one whose folder had already been reclaimed silently did nothing, ⌘K → New branch treated the archived name as taken and came back empty, and a relaunch could forget the branch outright. The branch is the git ref; the folder is a cache, cut again at its old path when you restore.

A project has to be a git repository with a branch. A plain folder used to land looking fine and then dead-end on "New branch", and picking a subdirectory quietly made a second project out of a repo you already had — that now resolves to the repository root, so re-adding reveals the project you have.
A notification's × closes it wherever you click the ×. Only a crescent of it was ever live; the middle answered nothing.

Closing a session takes its stray processes with it. A dev server an agent started in the background had been surviving the session, the app and reboots alike — measured at 3.6 GB across 34 processes.
Synth no longer crashes on launch when a project's folder has been moved, renamed or unmounted.

Browser comments arrive as one batch, not one interruption each. Comment mode queues: numbered pins accumulate on the page, a floating island owns the batch — count, target, one Send on ⌘⌥⏎ — and the agent receives a single numbered message with one viewport screenshot plus a clip per comment. A pin names an element rather than a coordinate, so it survives scrolling, resizing and zooming. Leaving the mode parks the batch instead of dropping it.

An agent you don't use is switched off, and Synth stops offering it. A switch per agent in Settings ▸ Synth ▸ Agent defaults drops it from every "New …" surface without touching a session already running one. Turning every agent off is allowed — the paths with no one in front of them say so up front rather than swallowing what you typed.

Every clean agent exit parks on the quit card. opencode exits 0 when it dies on its own, and the old "nothing to resume → close outright" rule silently deleted exactly the row you were watching. Any agent row that exits cleanly now lands on the Reopen card, resuming its session when one was captured. A shell's `exit` still closes a terminal row outright — there the clean exit is your gesture.

The 2px bar across an active split pane's top edge is gone. It was the heaviest rule in the window, spent on the least surprising fact on screen, and in tabs mode it sat a few pixels under a tab strip already drawing the same bar in the same colour. Which pane is active is still named where you look for it: the sidebar's copper tile and the active tab's own bar.

An agent that quits parks its conversation on a Reopen card. The row still leaves the tree, but it lands on an undo card — the agent's mark, the conversation's name, Reopen — and Reopen slots it back where it stood, rebuilding the pane with the conversation resumed. Unlike every other undo this card never drains: you didn't ask for it, and it can land while you're away.

Ctrl-C interrupts an opencode row, it doesn't quit it. opencode binds ctrl+c to app exit, so the universal stop gesture was ending the session outright and taking a long conversation with it. It's rebound inside Synth — ctrl+c interrupts, ctrl+d and the leader quit still quit — without touching any config file of yours.

Antigravity reports the states it stops in: a question, an interrupt, a cap, a failure. It shipped able to say only working or idle, so every other stop was reported as one of those and always the wrong one. A row blocked on a question now says so, a run you cancelled goes idle rather than red, and a hit limit reads as the error it is. Comments sent to a freshly-started Antigravity row also land reliably now, confirmed by the agent's own receipt rather than a guess at when its input was live.

Antigravity (`agy`) is Synth's third agent, alongside Claude Code and OpenCode — pick it when you start a session. It resumes where it left off, names its row from the conversation, and gets the browser tools like any other agent. A fresh worktree asks Antigravity's trust prompt first, so the row waits on you rather than swallowing what you typed.

A split's tabs are tabs again. Members had been shrunk to chips, which cost them the indicator dot — a pane needing input showed nothing — plus the active bar and hover. Each member is now a full tab, divided by a hairline, with an 8px map of the split in its corner showing which pane it is.

⌘K search ranks flat: typing gives one list scored against your query, best match on the top row. Results no longer bucket into Actions / Sessions / Branches / Projects, where the thing you wanted could sit six rows down under weaker siblings that shared its heading. Cold ⌘K keeps its groups.
Search scoring now gives exact and prefix label matches the boost they were meant to have, so typing a session or branch name lands it first.

Device previews are drawn from real hardware — true bezels, corner radii, cutout and safe areas, laid out at the device's own viewport and scaled to fit, so proportions hold at any pane width and rotating moves every edge one place round.

A previewed page now looks the way the phone's browser would show it: Safari's bottom tab bar in portrait, a single top bar in landscape, Chrome and a gesture pill on Android, a home button on the SE, and a status-bar trio that parts around the island.
The simulator pane takes its device from the session's name and gets an app's chrome rather than a browser's. Device screens stay light in both themes — it's a separate machine showing a light page.
The first tab's fill now runs under the sidebar instead of stopping square against its rounded edge, so the open tab no longer reads as clipped.
Notifications now order by what it costs to miss them rather than by severity — a needs-input from ten seconds ago no longer lands behind an error you dealt with minutes ago, ⌘↩ included.
A notification folded away under "+N" pauses its countdown, so a card can no longer expire having never been on screen.
Sidebar branch names leave the monospace for the app's own font, and the branch you're checked out on is visibly the one you're on again.
Sidebar rows hold their height: expanding a branch, or a branch going busy, no longer nudged every row below it by a couple of pixels mid-click.
In Light, dim terminal text — spinners, hints, timestamps — is readable again; it had been rendering at roughly half the contrast the dark theme gives the same thing.

⌘⇧T opens a scratch terminal: a full shell in the branch you're looking at, for the quick errand you don't want a session row for. The same chord dismisses it, and dismissing ends it — every summon is a fresh shell. Esc closes it too, but only at an idle prompt, so vim and other full-screen tools keep working.
Quitting or restarting while a scratch command is still running now says so and names it, instead of ending it quietly. Restart had skipped its confirmation entirely and installed over a running job.
The dim behind the scratch terminal is now tuned per theme — in Light it no longer flattened the whole app to grey — and Reduce Motion is honoured.
A fresh install now starts with the Synth-app MCP server on, so an agent can offer to branch off a worktree for you — creating one still raises a prompt only your Create click answers.
Archived-worktree clean-up is now on by default. It only ever reclaims a folder whose work is merged, clean and past its grace period, and holds it aside a fortnight before deleting anything.
If you never touched either of those two toggles, they switch themselves on at next launch — Settings turns them back off.

New installs no longer ship a shared setup script or default agent flags. Claude Code runs without --dangerously-skip-permissions unless you add it yourself in Settings. Settings you have already saved are untouched.
Archiving a worktree now removes it from the sidebar for good — it no longer reappeared once the undo window passed. Restore it any time from ⌘K → Archived.

A new build now announces itself: once an update has downloaded, Synth raises a notification — and a quiet reminder once a day while it waits — telling you it installs the next time you quit, so Restart is a shortcut rather than something you have to do. Settings → About says the same and offers the same Restart.
Pressing ⌘↩ on a notification whose action opens a confirmation no longer instantly answers it — the card asks first, as it should.
A long notification no longer truncates its own text.

Removing a worktree now archives it — instant, with an undo, and your files left untouched; restore it any time from ⌘K → Archived. Deleting a worktree from disk is a separate step that always confirms, and a background clean-up only ever reclaims a folder once its work is safely on a remote.

Notifications get a cleaner shape: every card carries a real action button — Open, Undo, Retry or Review — with its keyboard shortcut printed inside, plus a separate × to dismiss, so leaving a notification is no longer the same click as acting on it. Errors now show what actually went wrong.
Creating a worktree works again in a repository that has no remote.
A browser opening straight onto a page no longer gets stuck showing a blank address.
Notifications now stack instead of replacing each other — a new one no longer evicts an unread card, and each fades on its own timer.
Click a sidebar row and the keyboard goes to the sidebar: r / d / a and j / k act on the row you clicked straight away, while the session still opens in the pane — press ↵ or ⌘1 to dive in and type.
The terminal stays crisp when you drag Synth's window between monitors of different pixel density, instead of rendering blurry until the next relayout.
Tabs (experimental): double-click a tab to rename it, right-click for its command menu — the same gestures the sidebar rows already have.
Tabs (experimental): the sidebar's keyboard shortcuts stay on branches and no longer flip a branch's hidden session list.

The dark terminal surface goes back to Synth's near-black, flush with the app frame — the 0.12.1 change had left ghostty's lighter default showing in the padding band as a pale halo. Foreground and colours still come from Claude Code's own dark theme.
The dark terminal now uses ghostty's own default scheme instead of Synth's near-black card — the override only fought the surface, and Claude Code paints its own dark theme regardless.
The light terminal moves to a cool near-white to match Synth's chrome, dropping the warm cream edge, and a stray copper focus ring the top-edge bar had already replaced is gone.
Close a session with ⌘W instead of ⌘D — the chord every tab and browser app already uses. It's the same instant close with undo; only the key moved, and ⌘D is now free.

New experimental Tabs view mode, off by default behind a single Settings toggle: sessions leave the sidebar and open as tabs, one strip per branch, with a split shown as a bonded cluster of its tabs. Switch tabs with ⌘⇧[ / ⌘⇧], close with ⌘W. Turn it off and Synth is byte-for-byte what it is today.

Removing a worktree can no longer delete its folder from a single stray keypress. The confirm now opens on the safe choice, and delete-from-disk is never the pre-selected option — so ⌘D on a branch, or a reflexive Enter, keeps your files.

The command palette (⌘K) opens instantly again, and text fields — rename, feedback, search — focus with no delay even in a session with dozens of panes; a system password-autofill check had been quietly stalling every field.
Big sessions stay fluid: saving your layout, dragging rows, and opening a browser no longer hitch as the session tree grows.

Settings is now a flat, two-tab surface — Synth and the current project — laid over the live sidebar. Per-row Override switches replace the accordion, and notification sounds, MCP servers, analytics and About finally have a home.
A project's settings layer on top of the shared default rather than replacing it: it holds only its delta, shown over the shared base — an empty project is pure inheritance.
Adding a project takes just its default branch and always opens the folder picker — no branch multi-select, no typed path. Add more branches later, one at a time.
The light terminal moves to a cool near-white with its 16 colours rebuilt for even contrast, and Claude Code now follows Synth's appearance instead of running its own dark theme in a light window.
⌘K reliably focuses the command palette input again — it could silently fail to focus once a session had built up many panes.
Holding a bare modifier key — ⌘, ⌥, ⌃ or ⇧ on its own — no longer kills the app mid-session.
Every sidebar row now ends in two buttons: delete, plus the verb that row owns — + to add a worktree or session, ⋯ on a session. Bigger targets, and delete still asks first.
The liveness sphere is lit evenly from its core out to the rim, so it reads as a ball rather than a flat cluster of dots.

Browser tools keep working on a busy engine. A browser holding dozens of tabs used to fail every call with an opaque timeout; there are also new health and cookie tools, and snapshots can be scoped to a selector.
The working indicator is now a violet sphere that pulses outward in rings. Violet keeps it clearly apart from the blue needs-input mark, which the previous cyan lattice could resemble at a glance.
Synth now downloads as a disk image you drag into Applications. Running it straight from Downloads could leave it unable to find its own tooling, and on some Macs macOS refused to open it at all.
A working session now shows a cyan lattice that beats outward from its centre, replacing the amber dot — easier to tell apart from the blue unread mark, and it reads as alive at a glance.
Fixed a crash that could close Synth the moment a web page reached for Bluetooth.
Crashes are captured again instead of silently vanishing, so the ones that slip through get reported and fixed.
Toasts now anchor to the shell's corner and drain a countdown bar as they auto-dismiss — hover, or switching away from Synth, pauses the clock; input and error toasts stay until you act.
The active pane is marked with a top-edge bar in the mark's colour, and clicking anywhere in a pane focuses it.
A background branch keeps its split layout — switch away and back and the panes are still there.
Reorder drags mark the drop slot with a copper line instead of reshuffling the list under your cursor (sidebar and Settings templates).
Splits stay within one branch — a cross-branch drop now refuses instead of silently dropping the pane.
The in-app Changelog is a keyboard-driven two-pane sheet.
Split the content area into panes — drag a session onto an edge, or split by keyboard (⌘⇧+arrows); each branch remembers its own layout, ⌘⇧⏎ zooms a pane full-screen, and ⌘⇧U unsplits.
Browser page zoom (⌘+ / ⌘−), with a click-to-reset zoom badge in the address bar.
One command menu — the ⋯ kebab and right-click now match ⌘K, and negative actions (Close, Remove, Delete, Detach) are red.
Agents launch reliably even when your shell stops to ask about its own updates.
New worktrees fork off the default branch and start with no sessions.
Read what changed from the new in-app Changelog, and a fuller ⌘? shortcuts sheet.
Anonymous, opt-out product usage analytics — no login, no content on the wire, off on dev builds; turn it off in Settings → Privacy.
Native crash reporter so a crash is reported on the next launch.
Every quit now confirms with a single dialog, naming any busy sessions the quit would end.
Reissue of 0.4.0 — no functional changes.
Browser device mode (⌘⇧M) — render the page in a real device frame at true device viewports; agents can drive it too.
Pull-request indicators — each branch's PR state in the sidebar, and a clickable #number chip in the session header.
Copy the branch name from the pane header with one click.
Notifications now post from the open session, and the sidebar gets a restyle.
⌘D closes the current session — the focused sidebar row, or the open session — and Close always confirms first.
synth-app MCP server — agents can create worktrees with your approval and hand off to a fresh session; off by default, opt in from Settings.
Sidebar drops its indent guide lines — indentation alone carries the hierarchy.
⌘N opens the new-session picker for the branch you're in.
Browser sessions record video (browser_record_start / browser_record_stop).
Background self-updates, and a renderer that survives display changes.
First public release of Synth — an AI-first, Mac-native dev environment.
Sidebar of projects → branches → sessions with keyboard-first navigation and dark mode.
Embedded Ghostty terminals, Claude Code and OpenCode agents, and in-pane browser sessions.
Command palette (⌘K) for navigating and acting on anything, and a ⌘? shortcuts sheet.
Signed, notarized, self-updating builds.
